cultivation_relevance: Sorghum (Juwar) is a vital cereal and fodder crop in India, highly valued for its drought tolerance and resilience in semi-arid regions. In Gujarat, it plays a crucial role in providing staple food grain for rural populations and nutritious green fodder for livestock.

planting_details.sowing_time: Kharif: June-July (onset of monsoon); Rabi: September-October
planting_details.seed_rate: 8-10 kg per acre for grain; 16-20 kg per acre for fodder

nutrient_management.fym_manure_per_acre: 4 to 5 tonnes per acre applied during land preparation
nutrient_management.recommended_npk_ratio: N:P:K 32:16:0 kg per acre for grain (Rainfed); 40:20:0 kg per acre (Irrigated)
micronutrients: Zinc Sulphate (20 kg per acre if soil deficient)

harvest_and_yield.harvesting_signs: Hardening of grains, moisture content drops to 20-25%, yellowing of lower leaves
harvest_and_yield.expected_yield_per_acre: 8 to 12 quintals of grain; 30 to 40 quintals of dry fodder
harvest_and_yield.post_harvest_storage: Dry grains to safe moisture level below 12% before storing in hermetic bags or bins to prevent insect damage.
